_why: The harness scores every other guard in h-mad, so a hole here is invisible everywhere else. These target the machinery that turns 'something went red' into 'the named test bit' -- the discrimination `ALL_CAUGHT` structurally cannot express -- plus the anchor hints and the byte-compatibility of the summary line existing callers parse. Each mutation names the one test it is aimed at, which is also this feature dogfooding itself.

mutations.name: ignore-the-named-test-and-score-the-whole-suite
mutations._mechanism: Reverts to exit-code scoring. A mutant caught by an unrelated assertion then counts as a kill -- the exact blindness this feature closes.
mutations.find:
if target_command and mutation.get("test"):
                scoring_command = list(target_command) + [mutation["test"]]

mutations.name: a-wrong-catcher-counts-as-a-kill
mutations._mechanism: The named test passing is scored as caught anyway. Suite-red is treated as proof the property was exercised.

mutations.name: drop-the-red-pin-precheck
mutations._mechanism: L559: without it, a kill credited against a pin that was already failing measures nothing, and the whole-suite baseline cannot see a single red pin.

mutations.name: half-wired-spec-is-accepted-silently
mutations._mechanism: A `test` with no `target_command` would fall through to whole-suite scoring while the spec claims a per-test verdict that was never computed.
mutations.find: raise SpecError("a mutation names a `test` but the spec has no `target_command`")

mutations.name: accept-a-non-string-test-field
mutations._mechanism: A non-string nodeid would reach subprocess argv and fail as a launch error, which scores as red -- a fake kill.

mutations.name: drop-the-near-miss-hint
mutations._mechanism: L270: the REFUSED verdict stays correct but the recovery goes back to a manual re-grep for whatever the author's own edits moved.

mutations.name: near-miss-matches-the-whole-multiline-anchor
mutations._mechanism: Comparing a multi-line `find` against single lines finds nothing useful, so every hint degrades to 'no near miss' while looking implemented.

mutations.name: guess-a-near-miss-at-any-distance
mutations._mechanism: Dropping the cutoff makes every refusal produce a confident and unrelated suggestion -- worse than no hint, because it reads as an answer.
mutations.find: best = sorted((s for s in scored if s[0] >= 0.6), key=lambda s: (-s[0], s[1]))[:limit]
mutations.replace: best = sorted((s for s in scored if s[0] >= 0.0), key=lambda s: (-s[0], s[1]))[:limit]

mutations.name: ambiguous-anchor-gets-no-line-numbers
mutations._mechanism: The author is told the anchor matched N times but not where, which is the same manual re-grep in the other direction.

mutations.name: hints-are-computed-but-never-printed
mutations._mechanism: A result dict nobody can see. The CLI is the only surface an operator reads.
mutations.find:
for hint in hints.get(name, []):
            print(f"    hint: {hint}")

mutations.name: change-the-summary-line-callers-parse
mutations._mechanism: SKILL.md, failure-recovery.md and the codex verifier prompt all document this exact line. The additions must be detail lines only.

mutations.name: a-launch-failure-reads-as-green
mutations._mechanism: 'I could not measure' must never resolve to 'the guard is fine'. Pre-existing invariant, re-pinned because _run replaced _suite_is_green.

mutations.name: identical-lines-collapse-to-one-location
mutations._mechanism: `list.index()` on a de-duplicated candidate list reports the FIRST occurrence twice, so a line appearing at 1 and 3 is printed as 1 and 1. Found by dogfooding this spec against the harness itself.
mutations.find:
for i, ln in enumerate(lines)
        if ln.strip()
mutations.replace:
for i, ln in enumerate(lines)
        if ln.strip() and lines.index(ln) == i
